intent.title: Should we resume hedging the USD exposure, and how much of it?
intent.purpose: Settle the USD hedge after the forwards lapsed in April and the August move in SGD

outcome.question: Should we resume hedging the USD exposure, and how much of it?

options.name: Restore the policy hedge on USD
options.means: Roll monthly USD forwards again, sized to cover about 75 percent of the USD exposure as the rolls did until April (about 406 million USD of 542 million at the end of September).
for: Back inside the hedging range the investment policy sets; the exception note can be closed.
A repeat of the August move would cost about a quarter of what it cost this time.
against: Locks in USD at about 1.22 after SGD has already strengthened; part of the loss is behind us.
Brings back a running cost of about 0.8 to 1.1 million SGD a month, as in the last rolls.
options.needs: Mei Ling to reopen the forward line with the bank counterparty and roll on the first business day of each month.

notes.text: Policy says 70 to 90 percent on USD above 20 million. We are at zero. This is the clean answer from my side.

options.name: Hedge part now, step up over the quarter
options.means: Start with forwards on about 135 million USD in October and add the same each month of the fourth quarter towards the policy level, so we do not lock the whole exposure at one rate.
for: Cuts the open exposure by a quarter straight away.
Spreads the entry rate over three months instead of one day.
against: Still outside the policy range for October and November; the exception has to be extended.
Three dealing dates to manage instead of a single standing roll.
options.needs: Grace to extend the policy exception to 31 December; Mei Ling to size each step.

options.name: Stay unhedged and renew the exception
options.means: Keep the USD open for the next quarter because the family expects USD spending and capital calls, and record a formal exception to the hedging policy until 31 March 2027.
for: No hedging cost; about 11 million SGD a year at the old run rate.
USD capital calls on the private funds are paid from the same balances.
against: August alone cost about 47.2 million SGD on the open USD.
Outside policy since May; the committee asked for it to end.
options.needs: A signed exception from Grace and Daniel with a review date.

notes.text: I wrote this one down so it is on the record, not because I favour it.

history.note: Opened after the September FX numbers
